title.narrative: Working with Pastoralists and other minorities in Kenya towards Peacebuilding and Policy Advocacy

description.narrative:
CAFOD has established a working relationship with Centre for Minority Rights Development (CEMIRIDE) on peacebuilding and conflict transformation and advocacy based on their mutual experiences and strengths and targeting the marginalised pastoralist communities in Kenya. The project focuses on the poor and vulnerable communities in the ASAL regions. CEMIRIDE’s role in this partnership involved designing appropriate strategies to intervene in the post election crisis with respect to pastoralist communities and also formulating short and medium term strategies on peacebuilding and conflict transformation. CEMIRIDE in this project is also expected to build on the ongoing long-term work of some of CAFOD’s partners in the marginalised pastoralist areas of the country. The project would be implemented in three phases which included: 1-Rapid Assessment on the effects/impacts of the post election violence on the marginalised pastoralist communities. The assessment was conducted and the findings disseminated to a wider audience. This report’s findings have been useful in planning peacebuilding activities and other programmatic initiatives in the organization. For instance, the findings of the survey enabled CEMIRIDE and partners to appreciate the historical and immediate causes of insecurity in various parts of minority and indigenous people’s areas.
2-Short term intervention focusing on advocacy and peacebuilding and conflict transformation targeting Marsabit, Moyale, Samburu, Isiolo, Turkana South, West Pokot, Trans-Nzoia and the greater Kericho districts. These areas provided were targeted in the rapid assessment exercise whose findings have shaped CEMIRIDE’s engagement with the dioceses of Isiolo, Maralal and Marsabit on issues of advocacy and peacebuilding. This is set to be further consolidated in during the second year of the project.
3-Medium term intervention building on and consolidating the issues addressed in Phase 2 by building on the lessons and strengthening lobbying and advocacy as well as focused PBCT among the target pastoralist communities. Activities towards this purpose are projected to be implemented during this second year of the project especially concerted engagement with pastoralist parliamentary group, local community leaders, and media houses among others.
